ety.text: From Middle English feld, feeld (“field”), from Old English feld (“field”), from Proto-West Germanic *felþu (“field”), from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (“field”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“field, plain”) or *pleth₂- (“flat”) (with schwebeablaut).

senses.d: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; an area of open country.
ex: There are several species of wild flowers growing in this field.

senses.d: The open country near or belonging to a town or city.
A wide, open space that is used to grow crops or to hold farm animals, usually enclosed by a fence, hedge or other barrier.
ex: There were some cows grazing in a field.
A crop circle was made in a corn field.

senses.d: When coupled with a number (e.g. two-field) used to define types of crop rotation, denoting the number of different crop types (and possibly fallow) that are used.
A region containing a particular mineral.
ex: an oil field; a gold field

senses.d: An airfield, airport or air base; especially, one with unpaved runways.
A place where a battle is fought; a battlefield.
ex:
Tarry, sweet soul, for mine; then fly abreast,
As in this glorious and well-foughten field
We kept together in our chivalry!

senses.d: An area reserved for playing a game or race with one’s physical force.
ex: soccer field
Substitutes are only allowed onto the field after their boots are checked.

senses.d: The team in a match that throws the ball and tries to catch it when it is hit by the other team (the bat).
The outfield.
To intercept or catch (a ball) and play it.
To be the team catching and throwing the ball, as opposed to hitting it.
ex: The blue team are fielding first, while the reds are batting.

senses.d: To place (a team, its players, etc.) in a game.
ex: The away team fielded two new players and the second-choice goalkeeper.

senses.d: To answer; to address.
ex: She will field questions immediately after her presentation.

senses.d: To execute research (in the field).
ex: He fielded the marketing survey about the upcoming product.

senses.d: To deploy in the field.
ex: to field a new land-mine detector
